transcript: Once again, The Public Theater is serving the public with a traveling Shakespeare production. This year, they're doing Much Ado About Nothing, a one-act, bilingual, musical version, to be precise. As with the rest of their community Shakespeare initiatives, this is completely free to attend and requires no prior reservation. Much Ado About Nothing is one of Shakespeare's most well-known comedies, and features very Shakespearean plot points and themes like deception, mistaken identities, and witty romance. This production stars a small cast of actors, each making the most of their multiple characters and the playfulness of performing in a scrappy, outdoor staging. The Public's Mobile Unit is traveling around all five boroughs of New York through the end of the month, so it's definitely worth seeing if they'll be performing anywhere near you. The tour stop I went to was in Morningside Heights and it was actually packed, despite the cloudy and misty weather. In a time where getting folks into seats can be really difficult, it made me so happy to see such a great turnout for this — it really goes to show how people want to and will go to the theater, if it's accessible. With that, another program for my collection.
